# RL Task Quality rubric (source-decidable subset) - from RL_Task_QC_Scorecard.xlsx.
#
# 19 criteria kept: each decidable by READING the task's static source files
# (instruction.md, task.toml, solution/, tests/, environment/) - all the QC rubric judge gets.
# No run, trial, oracle or reward data exists at this stage.
#
# 11 scorecard criteria REMOVED as run/measurement-dependent: A4, B5, C1, C2, C3, D1, D3, D4, E1, F1, F4.
# Those belong in the execution / model_runs QC stages, which actually run the task.
#
# (Source sheet self-labels '34 criteria' but has 30 rows; ids A1, A5, B2 absent. Its weights
# and gate shading are not representable here - this stage is flat pass/fail.)

[[criteria]]
name = "derived_from_real_traffic_not_synthesised"
description = "Derived from real traffic, not synthesised"
guidance = """
Category: Prompt realism (scorecard id A2).

PASS (meets the bar): Verbatim or lightly-edited from a real arena/product log, with provenance recorded

FAIL: Model-generated prompts with no real-world source

Decide this ONLY from the task's source files. PASS if the criterion is met as described above; FAIL if it matches the failure description.
"""

guidance = """
Category: Prompt realism (scorecard id A3).

FAIL: Every prompt cleaned into polite full sentences

Decide this ONLY from the task's source files. PASS if the criterion is met as described above; FAIL if it matches the failure description.
"""

FAIL: Ambiguous, or asks for data/tools the environment does not have

Decide this ONLY from the task's source files. PASS if the criterion is met as described above; FAIL if it matches the failure description.
"""

guidance = """
Category: Verifier coverage (scorecard id B1).

guidance = """
Category: Determinism (scorecard id E2).

[[criteria]]

description = "Verifier runs offline or on a pinned allowlist"
guidance = """
Category: Determinism (scorecard id E3).

[[criteria]]
name = "judge_model_temperature_and_prompt_are_pinned"

Decide this ONLY from the task's source files. PASS if the criterion is met as described above; FAIL if it matches the failure description.

[[criteria]]
name = "judge_is_injection_resistant"
description = "Judge is injection-resistant"
guidance = """
Category: Anti-gaming (scorecard id F2).

PASS (meets the bar): Agent output cannot instruct the judge; tested with an injected directive

FAIL: Agent text is concatenated into the judge prompt unguarded

Decide this ONLY from the task's source files. PASS if the criterion is met as described above; FAIL if it matches the failure description.
"""

[[criteria]]
name = "tests_and_rubric_are_not_readable_by_the_agent"
description = "Tests and rubric are not readable by the agent"
guidance = """
Category: Anti-gaming (scorecard id F3).

PASS (meets the bar): Separate verifier environment; tests/ never uploaded to the agent container

FAIL: Agent can read the assertions it is graded on

Decide this ONLY from the task's source files. PASS if the criterion is met as described above; FAIL if it matches the failure description.
"""

Upload Checks (the QC "Rules" stage)
These are the built-in checks that run in the Upload checks (RULES) stage — the first stage of the QC pipeline. They validate a task's structure and metadata (task.toml, Dockerfiles, instruction.md, test.sh, solve.sh) at upload time, before anything runs in a sandbox. They are separate from your uploaded static-check scripts and from Rubric / Model Runs.

There are 26 checks across 5 categories.
How they run
The Rules stage is on_fail = "stop", so if any error-severity check fails, the whole pipeline halts and Static Checks / Rubric / Model Runs are skipped.
Each check has a default severity. A project can raise, lower, or turn off any unlocked check; a locked check's severity cannot be changed (it guards a correctness invariant).
Severity
Severity | Meaning
error | Blocks the task (fails the version, stops the pipeline).
warning | Reported in the grid, does not block.
off | Not run at all.
Changing severity (no UI yet — API only)
There is currently no settings screen for this; the endpoint exists but the editor isn't wired. Set an override with a PUT (project-wide; a revalidation job re-scores existing tasks):

curl -X PUT 'https://eval.agentic.turing.com/api/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/validation-policy' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"checks": {"check-pip-pinning": {"severity": "warning"}}}'

config values (e.g. timeouts, allowed GPU types, required fields) are tuned the same way, via {"checks": {"<id>": {"config": {...}}}} — locked checks accept only their unlocked_config keys.


Environment & image (8)
check-task-timeout — Timeouts are numeric and within cap  ·  error · 🔒 locked
[agent]/[verifier] timeout_sec must be a positive number. max_timeout_sec caps a single phase; max_total_timeout_sec caps build + agent + verifier together and must match the sandbox age limit, or a task that passes here is deleted mid-run for being too old. Tunable (even though locked): max_timeout_sec (default 18000), max_total_timeout_sec (21600).
check-sandbox-resources — Sandbox fits provisioning limits  ·  error · 🔒 locked
[environment] cpus / memory_mb / storage_mb must fit a single Daytona sandbox. GPU tasks get a larger per-GPU allowance. Raise these only after raising them in Daytona. Tunable: max_cpu_per_sandbox (4), max_memory_gib_per_sandbox (8), max_disk_gib_per_sandbox (10), max_cpu_per_gpu (16), max_memory_gib_per_gpu (192), max_disk_gib_per_gpu (512).
check-dockerfile-references — Agent image excludes solution and tests  ·  error · 🔒 locked
An agent able to read the solution invalidates every score the task produces.
check-network-mode — Network posture  ·  error
What network access tasks may have. Modes: public (default), no-network, allowlist. A task more permissive than the project requires is flagged; a stricter one is only noted. Reads [environment].network_mode plus [agent]/[verifier] phase overrides. Legacy allow_internet is understood. Set to Off if the project has no opinion. Config: required_mode (public), exempt_tasks ([]).
check-allowed-hosts — Allowlist mode declares its hosts  ·  error
network_mode = "allowlist" with no allowed_hosts leaves the reachable set undefined, so behaviour depends on the backend rather than the task.
check-gpu-types — GPU types are recognised  ·  error
GPU values must match what the execution backend accepts. Config: allowed_gpu_types = T4, L4, A10, L40S, A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100, H200, B200, any.
check-dockerfile-platform — No --platform pin in FROM  ·  error
Pinning an architecture stops the task running on other backends.
check-compose-host-binds — Compose uses named volumes, not host binds  ·  error
Host bind mounts don't exist inside a sandboxed backend, so a task that relies on one silently loses its data.


Reproducibility (6)
check-base-image-pinned — Base image is pinned  ·  error
FROM with no tag means :latest, so the image changes without warning and the task scores differently on a rebuild. Pin a tag, or a digest for an exact guarantee. Config: require_digest (false).
check-nproc — No bare nproc  ·  error
Inside a container nproc reports the host CPU count, so make -j$(nproc) over-parallelises and gets OOM-killed.
check-pip-pinning — pip installs are version-pinned  ·  error
Unpinned installs drift after the task is authored, so a rebuild months later scores differently. Scans environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, solution/solve.sh for pip install …, uvx --with …, uv tool install … without a ==<version> pin.
check-dockerfile-sanity — Dockerfile apt hygiene  ·  error
Fail on version-pinned apt packages (they break as repos update); warn on missing apt-get update or missing rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleanup.
check-pytest-version — Pinned test-tool versions  ·  error
Hold every task to one pytest / pytest-json-ctrf version so verifier behaviour is uniform. Blank means no opinion. Config: pytest (8.3.4), pytest_json_ctrf (0.3.6).
check-trial-network-fetch — Verifier does not fetch at trial time  ·  error
curl | sh, wget, or git clone inside tests/test.sh makes scoring depend on the network being up and unchanged. Separate mode only.


Metadata & naming (5)
check-canary — Canary string present  ·  off by default
A unique marker embedded in every text file. On an eval set it detects contamination (leak into a training corpus); on a training set it's provenance. Set your own string; blank disables it. Config: canary_string (''), require_comment (true).
check-task-fields — Required task.toml metadata  ·  off by default
Required [metadata] keys, category from the taxonomy, and non-empty subcategory. Config: required_fields = difficulty_explanation, solution_explanation, category, subcategory, persona; valid_categories = Science, Software, ML, Operations, Security, Hardware, Media.
check-task-slug — Task folder name shape  ·  error
Caps how many hyphen-separated words a folder name may use (long names get unwieldy in logs/paths). Config: max_tokens (8), require_kebab_case (false).
check-task-version — Task package version is declared  ·  off by default
Harbor 0.21.0 added [task] version (the task's own release number, 1.0.0 for new tasks — not schema_version). Ships off; turn on once authors produce versioned tasks. Config: require_semver (false).
check-task-package-name — Task name uses an org prefix  ·  error
Require [task] name to read <org>/<folder> so published tasks resolve under one namespace. Blank disables it. Config: org (turing).


Instructions (3)
check-instruction-suffix — Instruction ends with a required sentence  ·  off by default
Appends a house rule to every instruction (typically the timeout + an anti-cheat line). Use {timeout} for the agent timeout. Blank disables it. Config: template ('').
check-task-absolute-path — Instructions use absolute paths  ·  off by default
Flags relative file paths in instruction.md that should be absolute under the container working dir.
check-test-file-references — Test outputs are named in the instruction  ·  error
Files referenced by both tests and the solution must be mentioned in instruction.md or task.toml.


Verifier (4)
check-test-sh-sanity — Shared-verifier test.sh mentions uv, npm or pnpm  ·  off by default
In shared mode, test.sh should isolate via uv/npm/npx/pnpm, or declare a system-wide install. Separate mode skips this.
check-verifier-tooling-baked — Separate verifier bakes its own tooling  ·  error
In separate mode the test runner belongs in tests/Dockerfile, not installed at trial time.
check-artifact-paths — Artifact entries are collectable  ·  error
Harbor 0.21.0 validates artifacts at load: source/destination may not contain .., destination must be a relative forward-slash path and not named manifest.json, and a sidecar-service entry needs an absolute source. Entries landing on the same host path are reported as a warning (first kept, rest skipped).
check-separate-verifier — Separate verifier is fully configured  ·  off by default
environment_mode must be "separate", artifacts top-level, and tests/Dockerfile with COPY/ADD into /tests plus mkdir for artifact parents.

Top-level artifacts are absolute /app and /logs/verifier; no .., explicit destination collision, reserved manifest.json destination or sidecar entry. Source-form review only, not Harbor loader execution.

Separate mode, top-level artifacts and COPY . /tests are present. tests/Dockerfile does not explicitly mkdir /app and /logs/verifier artifact parents; test.sh creates logs at runtime. The documented optional strict image rule may require image-time parent creation if enabled.
